### Observed differences

- The clearest differences concentrate on A02, A09 and A06. In the earlier window, A02 and A09 each appeared in about 21 in 100 traces (roughly 0.34 occurrences per trace); in the later window they appear in about 27 in 100 traces (roughly 0.6 occurrences per trace), and the share of traces containing a repeat of the activity rose from about 10 to 16 in 100. A06 rose from about 18 to 23 in 100 traces and from about 0.36 to 0.66 occurrences per trace, with repeats up from about 9 to 15.5 in 100. A07, A08, A10 and A11 moved in the same direction more weakly (for example A07 from about 29.5 to 34 in 100 traces). A01 (present in every trace in both windows), A03, A04 and A05 were essentially stable in participation. [OCC002, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010, OCC001, OCC003, OCC004, REL002]

- Routing between these activities shifted. From A02, the share of outgoing transitions to A09 rose from about 45% to 57%, while the share to A07 fell from about 36% to 21%. From A09, the share to A06 rose from about 19% to 32% and the share back to A02 fell from about 55% to 42%. From A06, the share to A02 rose from about 17% to 27%; from A11, the share to A06 rose from about 45% to 58%. These shares rest on 67–131 observed outgoing transitions per window. [DIR002, DIR007, DIR005, DIR009]

- The cluster's activities increasingly share traces: A02–A09 co-occurrence rose from 21 to 27 in 100 traces, A02–A06 from 15 to 22, A06–A09 from 15 to 22 and A02–A10 from about 10 to 16.5 in 100; A02 and A09 still never appear without one another in either window. [REL017, REL014, REL043, REL018]

- Secondary differences: A03 follows A01 at the next event position in about 76% of close A01–A03 pairs in the later window, up from about 67%; A02, A06 and A09 occur at slightly later relative positions (A09 mean relative position about 0.43 to 0.49); a few edges appear or vanish with single observations (A02→A04 and A09→A04 once each in the later window, A11→A04 no longer observed), which is rare-variant level noise; and many remaining pair-distance items rest on fewer than about 20 observed pairs. [LAG003, POS002, POS005, POS008, DIR002, DIR007, DIR009, LAG018, LAG019, LAG094]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

In the later window, the repeating segment involving A02, A09 and A06 was executed more often and in more cases: A02 and A09 (which always occur together) rose from about 21 to 27 in 100 traces and from about 0.34 to 0.6 occurrences per trace, A06 rose from about 18 to 23 in 100 traces and from about 0.36 to 0.66 occurrences, and within-trace repetition increased for all three. The routing shifts point the same way — from A02 more often on to A09 and less often to A07, from A09 more often to A06 and less often directly back to A02, from A06 more often back to A02, and from A11 more often into A06 — so the evidence reads as existing paths being taken with different frequencies and the segment repeating more, not as an activity being added, removed, skipped or relocated. [OCC002, OCC005, OCC008, DIR002, DIR005, DIR007, DIR009, REL014, REL017, REL043]

Supporting signs: the occurrence, recurrence and routing evidence is direct and consistent, all of it pointing at the same four activities; the two main routing shifts rest on 67 → 118 outgoing transitions, with differences larger than all but about 1 in 20 (A02) and 1 in 10 (A09) of random re-splits, and the position shifts of A02, A06 and A09 are consistent with the added later-trace repetitions rather than a relocation. Limitations: the evidence contains no screening baseline, so the number of qualifying items cannot be checked against the number expected if nothing had changed; many relation items simply restate the occurrence figures (co-occurrence with the ever-present A01 equals participation), so they do not add independent weight. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the routing shifts are a mechanical by-product of more repetitions per trace (relatively more mid-loop transitions) rather than a change in the choice probabilities between the exits. [DIR002, DIR007, POS002, POS005, POS008, OCC002, OCC005, OCC008]

Other differences: A03 now follows A01 more immediately than before, and A04 and A05 participation dipped slightly (about 48.5 to 45 and 33.5 to 30 in 100 traces) without notable strength. [LAG003, OCC003, OCC004]
